Windows may be restarting automatically when you're not at the computer, closing IdleOn, and ruining your *active idling* sessions.

# Why Active Idle?
There are some bonuses in the game that only work when the game is running and you are logged into the character, usually with the character toggled on `Auto`. DK talents and the faster portal opening from the Upgrade Vault come to mind. This is `Active Idling`; instead of `AFK Idling` which is when you are logged out of a character or the game is closed.

# Why is Windows restarting automatically?
Windows is restarting automatically when it believes you are not at your computer to finish applying important Windows Updates.

## Why not turn off Windows Update completely?
Some people may suggest turning the Windows Update service off to stop this. In general this is a very bad ideal. I'm sure you're the exception, but almost everyone forgets to turn it back on regularly to apply updates, which can be very bad. Don't do this.

## Why should I restart Windows regularly?
They often fix bugs that cause problems with your games, programs, or computer. Sometimes security fixes are done that stop your computer from getting infected with viruses. Many windows updates require a computer restart to be applied, hence, if you want regular updates, you have to regularly restart. 

## How often should I be restarting Windows?
Ideally as soon as possible after any critical update. That is why windows automatically does it "nightly". Since we're going to turn off automatic restarts, I would say at the very least monthly, if not weekly.

# Turning automatic restarts off

## Where to find the settings
You will need to do some of your own research, we can't cover every version or setting location for Windows. Each version and edition of windows will likely have different settings worded differently in different places. Windows 11 Pro is different than Windows 11 Home, different still from the same two in Windows 10. **I will not be helping you troubleshoot where to find the settings. You'll have to look for yourself, I don't have your version of windows, I can't find it.**

## Windows Update settings
First, under `Windows Update settings`, you can usually find a `Advanced options` section that says something similar to `Notify when a restart is required to finish updating`. Just turning this on may reduce the frequency windows reboots without your input, but not completely.

## Local Group Policy Editor
This program is for companies to manage their computers, and has many settings you won't find in the regular UI. You may not have this program installed if you don't have the `Pro` variant of windows. Try finding it by typing `Local Group Policy Editor` in your start menu. Other times you'll need to launch it from a `Run with Administrator` privileged command window by typing `gpedit.msc`. You can then find settings under `Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Windows Update` that allow you to control when windows restarts your computer. Two important folders to look in are the `Manage end user experience` and `Legacy Policies` folders. `No auto-restart with logged on users for scheduled automatic updates installation` is a key one to change if you can find it.

### Installing Local Group Policy Editor in `Home` windows versions
If you don't have the program, perhaps because you have the `Home` variant of windows, you may be able to still install it using a command prompt (not powershell). It may not work for you. See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/3842434/how-to-enable-the-gpedit-msc-on-windows-10-and-11?forum=windows-all

# Further research
If you've tried the above and are still stuck, you'll need to do your own research, but you know the goal now. **I will not be helping you troubleshoot where to find the settings. You'll have to look for yourself, I don't have your version of windows, I can't find it.** A good starting point to find a discussion about this and various solutions people found for their specific versions of windows can be found at the winaero configuration tool website, and in this wiki thread: 
https://winaero.com/how-to-disable-windows-update-in-windows-10-rtm/
https://superuser.com/questions/1817039/disable-automatic-restarts-windows-11

Good luck and hopefully this helps you! 

**Please keep the comment section for corrections and updates to the above guide, instead of requests for help.**
